newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO agrees MeesPierson sale to Fortis.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO agrees MeesPierson sale to Fortis.

text.p: The Netherlands's largest bank ABN AMRO said on Friday it had signed a letter of intent to sell its MeesPierson investment bank unit to Belgian/Dutch financial group Fortis.
Fortis and ABN AMRO said in a joint statement that they expected it would take about two months before an agreement could be signed.
No financial details were given but the deal has been well flagged by analysts, who reckoned it could be worth as much as 2.5 billion guilders ($1.46 billion).
Fortis said the acquisition "would mean a significant step forward in its growth strategy. MeesPierson offers Fortis complementary activities in attractive growth markets."
ABN AMRO said it was convinced that MeesPierson's growth potential was best served as a member of the Fortis group.

MeesPierson, which employs 4,000 staff, has over 50 billion guilders of assets under management. It has main offices in Amsterdam, Rotterdam and The Hague, and subsidiaries elsewhere in Europe, the Far East and the United States.
Its Dutch units include brokers Theodoor Gilissen and H. Wesselius & Co.
MeesPierson posted 1995 operating profits of 182 million guilders. Net profit was 250 million guilders.
The investment bank unit was created in April 1993 through amerger of ABN AMRO's subsidiaries Bank Mees & Hope and Pierson, Heldring & Pierson. ($1=1.717 Guilder)
